intro: OpenAI and Nvidia both push new inference silicon into production the same week, Anthropic and Slack rework how coding agents fit into daily workflows, and bitcoin's ETF-fueled rally clears $81,000.

items.headline: Claude's memory now follows you between chat and Cowork
items.summary: Anthropic merged Claude's memory system so context learned on one surface, chat or the Cowork agent, carries over to the other, replacing the old end-of-conversation summary with continuously updated, categorized entries.
items.why: Cuts the repeated re-briefing that made switching between Claude surfaces annoying for teams running long projects.

items.headline: Slack launches dedicated channels for coding agents
items.summary: Slack Code gives teams project-specific channels where Claude Code, Devin, GitHub Copilot and Vercel's agent work alongside humans, proposing diffs and live previews and waiting for sign-off before anything ships.
items.why: Pushes agentic coding out of solo terminal sessions and into a reviewable, team-visible workflow.

items.headline: Shopify's CEO threatens to ban Claude Code over AGENTS.md
items.summary: Tobi Lutke said he's considering banning Claude Code at Shopify because it still won't natively read AGENTS.md, the cross-tool agent-instructions file now used by more than 60,000 open-source projects; Anthropic has so far declined the feature request.
items.why: A live flashpoint in the fight over which agent-config standard becomes the default.

items.headline: OpenAI's first custom chip posts inference numbers that beat Nvidia's best
items.summary: OpenAI and Broadcom's Jalapeno inference chip topped SemiAnalysis' InferenceX benchmark on both tokens-per-user and throughput-per-kilowatt, the first hard data point behind OpenAI's push to cut its dependence on Nvidia GPUs.
items.why: If the numbers hold up at scale, it's a real crack in Nvidia's inference monopoly, not just a chip announcement.

items.headline: Nvidia's Groq 3 LPX inference chip enters full production
items.summary: Nvidia's purpose-built inference accelerator, an extension of the Vera Rubin platform, is now shipping with Nebius as the first cloud to deploy it; Nvidia says it hit the fastest token-generation speeds ever recorded running Gemma 4 31B.
items.why: Nvidia's direct answer to the custom-silicon moves from OpenAI/Broadcom and Google/Anthropic; the inference-chip race is now a multi-way fight.

items.headline: Jetpack Compose 1.12 ships with mesh gradients, Views-level startup speed
items.summary: Google's Compose 1.12 release bumps compileSdk to API 37, adds a MeshGradientPainter for organic multi-point gradients, and closes the gap on Time to Initial Display versus the older Android Views system.
items.why: Startup-time parity with Views removes one of the last reasons teams delay a Compose migration.

items.headline: SvelteKit 3 preview lands with reorganized $app modules
items.summary: The SvelteKit 3 preview reorganizes the framework's $app modules and ships zero-config error props and a refreshAll helper, alongside smaller releases adding submitted-state tracking for remote forms.
items.why: Signals where the framework is headed as it moves toward a major version.

items.headline: Bitcoin briefly tops $81,000 as ETF inflows hit a seventh straight day
items.summary: Bitcoin extended its rally to briefly clear $81,000 on August 25 as U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs logged a seventh consecutive day of net inflows, holding the broader move above $80,000.
items.why: Sustained ETF buying, not just spot speculation, is what's underpinning the move.

items.headline: Bitcoin and ether ETFs pull in $2.6B in their strongest week since October
items.summary: Combined spot bitcoin and ether ETF inflows hit $2.6 billion for the week, the category's best since October, with trading volume more than tripling to $29 billion as the rally accelerated.
items.why: Confirms the rally is being driven by real institutional flow, not just thin-volume speculation.
